objectives.text: Trace a bite of food through the GI tract and name what happens at each stop.
Distinguish mechanical from chemical digestion, and digestion from absorption.
Say where most absorption happens and what makes that surface suited to it.
Explain what a calorie measures and how energy reaches the cell.
Describe common GI disorders and the dietary change each calls for.

terms.gloss: Physical breakdown — chewing, churning — that increases surface area without changing chemistry.
Enzymes and acid splitting molecules into absorbable units.
Movement of nutrients across the gut lining into blood or lymph. Digestion prepares; absorption delivers.
Finger-like projections of the small-intestine lining that multiply its absorptive surface.
Coordinated muscle waves that move contents along the tract.
Energy to raise one kilogram of water by one degree Celsius. A food 'Calorie' is a kilocalorie.

questions.prompt: Where does most nutrient absorption take place?
questions.why: The small intestine's folds, villi and microvilli give it an enormous surface area, and that is where most nutrients cross into the body.
distractorNotes: Mainly chemical digestion and mixing; little absorption.
Absorbs water and some vitamins, not most nutrients.
A transport tube — no absorption at all.

questions.prompt: Chewing a piece of bread is an example of:
questions.why: Chewing breaks food apart physically and raises surface area. The salivary amylase acting at the same time is the chemical half.
distractorNotes: That is the enzyme's work, not the teeth's.
Nothing has crossed the gut wall yet.
Muscle waves further down the tract.

options: Slowing the passage of food along
questions.why: Absorption scales with contact area. Folds, villi and microvilli each multiply it, turning a modest tube into a very large absorptive surface.
distractorNotes: Enzymes come largely from the pancreas and lining cells.
Motility is controlled separately.
Pancreatic bicarbonate does the neutralising.

questions.prompt: A food Calorie, written with a capital C, is equal to:
questions.why: The food Calorie is a kilocalorie — a thousand small calories. It is why label figures look small next to the physics unit.
distractorNotes: That is the small calorie, a thousand times less.
Off by a factor of a million.
A joule is a different and much smaller unit.

questions.prompt: What is the stomach's main contribution to digestion?
questions.why: The stomach mixes, acidifies and begins protein digestion, releasing the result gradually into the small intestine.
distractorNotes: Very little absorption happens there.
The direction is reversed — acid leaves the stomach.
Bile is stored in the gallbladder.

questions.prompt: Someone with lactose intolerance lacks enough of which enzyme?
questions.why: Lactase splits lactose. Without enough of it, the sugar reaches the colon undigested and is fermented by bacteria there.
distractorNotes: Lactose is the sugar itself, not the enzyme.
Amylase acts on starch.
Pepsin acts on protein.

questions.prompt: Digestion and absorption differ in that:
options: Digestion breaks down, absorption takes up
Digestion happens only in the stomach
questions.why: Digestion reduces food to units small enough to cross the gut wall; absorption is that crossing. One prepares, the other delivers.
distractorNotes: Digestion is both mechanical and chemical.
It begins in the mouth and continues well past the stomach.
The order is the other way round.

questions.prompt: What is the main job of the large intestine?
options: Digesting the bulk of the protein
questions.why: By the time contents arrive, most nutrients are gone. The colon reclaims water and electrolytes, and its bacteria ferment what remains.
distractorNotes: Protein digestion finishes well upstream.
Fat absorption is a small-intestine job.
Those come from salivary glands and pancreas.

questions.prompt: Which dietary change most directly addresses ordinary constipation?
questions.why: Fibre adds bulk and holds water, and the water has to be there for it to work. Fibre without fluid can make matters worse.
distractorNotes: Removes exactly what adds bulk.
Protein does not address bulk or hydration.
Refining strips the fibre out.

questions.prompt: Energy from food becomes usable to a cell only after:
options: Food has been chewed very thoroughly
Food has been acidified in the stomach
Fibre is fermented in the colon
questions.why: A calorie on a label is potential energy. The cell can use it only once the nutrient is absorbed and run through metabolism.
distractorNotes: A useful first step, but far from sufficient.
Also only a step along the way.
Fermentation yields a modest amount, not the main route.

checklist: Pick one meal you ate and follow it from mouth to colon.
At each stop, name what acts on it and what it becomes.
Say where each of its macronutrients is absorbed.
Name one disorder that would disrupt this path, and where.
selfCheck: Did I separate mechanical from chemical at each stop?
Did I say where absorption happens, not just digestion?
applicationPrompts.aiPolicy: These are questions for you to answer. This app does not write any part of a submission.
